fact_check_rounds.label: Round 1: the 40 profiled top-ranked plants (one checker per profiler batch, on the unmerged profiler files)
Cross-vertical checks (state air permits, job-board dates, OSHA headcounts, profiles of OSHA top-40 entrants): rows for this vertical's plants

miss_rate.note: R2 blind audit after closure 3: 5 verified misses / (30 included plants the auditors found + 5). Auditors: job postings (C) and project records, supplier awards and MBI lists (D); neither reached a dry point. Against the list before closure 3: 7/35 = 20.0%. Upper bound counting 5 company-level or city-less candidates as misses: 10/40 = 25.0%.

known_limits: Neither blind audit reached a dry point in either round; the R2 upper bound is 25.0%.
The large-switchgear rule first existed only in a verifier brief written after the R1 candidate names were known; rubric R1-R6 was written down (consultation 27) before closure 3 and the R2 audit.

Closure 3 screened 1,030 OSHA and sister-site rows; the 616 with no in-scope evidence are logged in ledger/audit/dc-closure3-screen-*.json rather than as excluded records, and about 63 switchgear rows could not be read (sites unreachable or nearly empty).
Sister sites of the largest parents (Eaton, Siemens, ABB, Schneider, Flex, Hubbell, Legrand, Mitsubishi) were mostly screened from the OSHA record alone.
Weld process scores 0 at the nVent sites and several switchgear plants because their postings say 'weld' without naming MIG or flux-core: unknown, not absent.

Several scores rest on city-only posting ties to the only registry record (nVent Houston, Vertiv Pelzer and Anderson, FTI Olathe, Vertiv Ironton, Crusoe Arvada, BASX Redmond): points kept, no confidence. Eaton Greenwood's five welder postings earn 0 because Eaton runs other buildings in the same ZIP.
Steel is not shown at some rack, cooling and switchgear plants (Vertiv Anderson's welding evidence is aluminum; Rittal Urbana and Vertiv Ironton do not state the metal).
